title: The Empty Party
text: On June twenty-eighth, 2009, Stephen Hawking threw a party for guests from the future, and not one of them came.

title: The Paradox
text: If the equations allowed these loops, why did Hawking want to shut them down? Because backward travel brings paradoxes. Consider the grandfather paradox.
nxt: An inventor builds a machine, travels back to when their grandfather was a child, and accidentally stops their grandparents from ever meeting.

title: The Paradox
text: Such contradictions attack the foundation of science, which is causality. A cause must come before its effect. You strike a match, and then the flame appears.
nxt: You drop an egg, and then it breaks. If effects could come before causes, a shattered egg could jump back into your hand.

title: Two Rulebooks

nxt: Quantum mechanics governs atoms. Each works brilliantly alone. At the edge of a time machine, they collide.

title: Escape Hatches
text: Some physicists try another escape. The Russian physicist Igor Novikov suggested that if loops exist, only self-consistent histories could happen.
nxt: Nothing you did in the past could ever contradict what already occurred. Researchers have found mathematical examples of this with colliding billiard balls.
